tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

42	extension Annotation {

55	    /// Returns a copy with the given color; unchanged for colorless types
56	    func withColor(_ newColor: AnnotationColor) -> Annotation {

100	    func moving(_ handle: AnnotationHandle, to point: CGPoint) -> Annotation {
101	        switch self {
102	        case .arrow(let from, let to, let color):
103	            return handle == .from
104	                ? .arrow(from: point, to: to, color: color)
105	                : .arrow(from: from, to: point, color: color)
106	        case .line(let from, let to, let color):
107	            return handle == .from
108	                ? .line(from: point, to: to, color: color)
109	                : .line(from: from, to: point, color: color)
110	        case .rectangle(let rect, let color):
111	            let anchor = oppositeCorner(of: handle, in: rect)

113	        case .ellipse(let rect, let color):

118	            return .crop(rect: rectFromCorners(anchor, point))
119	        case .blur(let rect):

122	        case .text(let origin, let width, let content, let fontSize, let color):
123	            if handle == .left {

141	    func offsetBy(dx: CGFloat, dy: CGFloat) -> Annotation {
142	        switch self {
143	        case .arrow(let from, let to, let color):
144	            return .arrow(
145	                from: CGPoint(x: from.x + dx, y: from.y + dy),
146	                to: CGPoint(x: to.x + dx, y: to.y + dy),
147	                color: color
148	            )
149	        case .line(let from, let to, let color):
150	            return .line(
151	                from: CGPoint(x: from.x + dx, y: from.y + dy),
152	                to: CGPoint(x: to.x + dx, y: to.y + dy),
153	                color: color
154	            )
155	        case .rectangle(let rect, let color):
156	            return .rectangle(rect: rect.offsetBy(dx: dx, dy: dy), color: color)
157	        case .ellipse(let rect, let color):
158	            return .ellipse(rect: rect.offsetBy(dx: dx, dy: dy), color: color)
159	        case .crop(let rect):
160	            return .crop(rect: rect.offsetBy(dx: dx, dy: dy))
161	        case .blur(let rect):

163	        case .text(let origin, let width, let content, let fontSize, let color):
164	            return .text(
165	                origin: CGPoint(x: origin.x + dx, y: origin.y + dy),
166	                width: width, content: content, fontSize: fontSize, color: color
167	            )
168	        case .badge(let center, let number, let color):
169	            return .badge(
170	                center: CGPoint(x: center.x + dx, y: center.y + dy),
171	                number: number, color: color
172	            )
173	        }

176	    /// Returns true if the given screenshot-space point hits this annotation's body
177	    func bodyContains(_ point: CGPoint, hitRadius: CGFloat) -> Bool {
178	        switch self {
179	        case .arrow(let from, let to, _), .line(let from, let to, _):
180	            return distanceToSegment(point: point, a: from, b: to) <= hitRadius
181	        case .rectangle(let rect, _), .crop(let rect), .blur(let rect):
182	            return rect.contains(point)
183	        case .ellipse(let rect, _):
184	            let halfWidth = rect.width / 2 + hitRadius
185	            let halfHeight = rect.height / 2 + hitRadius
186	            guard halfWidth > 0, halfHeight > 0 else { return false }
187	            let nx = (point.x - rect.midX) / halfWidth
188	            let ny = (point.y - rect.midY) / halfHeight
189	            return nx * nx + ny * ny <= 1
190	        case .text(let origin, let width, let content, let fontSize, _):
191	            let rect = Annotation.textBoundingRect(
192	                origin: origin, width: width, content: content, fontSize: fontSize
193	            )
194	            return rect.contains(point)
195	        case .badge(let center, _, _):
196	            return hypot(point.x - center.x, point.y - center.y) <= Annotation.badgeRadius + hitRadius
197	        }
198	    }
199	
200	    private func distanceToSegment(point: CGPoint, a: CGPoint, b: CGPoint) -> CGFloat {
201	        let abx = b.x - a.x
202	        let aby = b.y - a.y
203	        let lengthSq = abx * abx + aby * aby
204	        if lengthSq == 0 { return hypot(point.x - a.x, point.y - a.y) }
205	        let t = max(0, min(1, ((point.x - a.x) * abx + (point.y - a.y) * aby) / lengthSq))
206	        let closestX = a.x + t * abx
207	        let closestY = a.y + t * aby
208	        return hypot(point.x - closestX, point.y - closestY)
209	    }
210	
211	    private struct TextHeightCacheKey: Hashable {
212	        let width: CGFloat
213	        let content: String
214	        let fontSize: CGFloat
215	    }
216	
217	    private static var textHeightCache: [TextHeightCacheKey: CGFloat] = [:]
218	
219	    static func textBoundingRect(
220	        origin: CGPoint, width: CGFloat, content: String, fontSize: CGFloat
221	    ) -> CGRect {
222	        let cacheKey = TextHeightCacheKey(width: width, content: content, fontSize: fontSize)
223	        let height: CGFloat
224	        if let cached = textHeightCache[cacheKey] {
225	            height = cached
226	        } else {
227	            let font = NSFont.boldSystemFont(ofSize: fontSize)
228	            let attrs: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [.font: font]
229	            let boundingSize = CGSize(width: width, height: CGFloat.greatestFiniteMagnitude)
230	            let textRect = (content as NSString).boundingRect(
231	                with: boundingSize, options: [.usesLineFragmentOrigin, .usesFontLeading],
232	                attributes: attrs
233	            )
234	            height = max(textRect.height, fontSize * 1.5)
235	            textHeightCache[cacheKey] = height
236	        }
237	        return CGRect(x: origin.x, y: origin.y, width: width, height: height)
238	    }
239	
240	    private func oppositeCorner(of handle: AnnotationHandle, in rect: CGRect) -> CGPoint {
241	        switch handle {
242	        case .topLeft: return CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: rect.maxY)
243	        case .topRight: return CGPoint(x: rect.minX, y: rect.maxY)
244	        case .bottomLeft: return CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: rect.minY)
245	        case .bottomRight: return CGPoint(x: rect.minX, y: rect.minY)
246	        default: return CGPoint(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY)
247	        }
248	    }
249	
250	    private func rectFromCorners(_ a: CGPoint, _ b: CGPoint) -> CGRect {
251	        CGRect(
252	            x: min(a.x, b.x),
253	            y: min(a.y, b.y),
254	            width: abs(b.x - a.x),
255	            height: abs(b.y - a.y)
256	        )
257	    }
258	}

96	    /// Converts a view-space point to screenshot coordinates
97	    func viewToScreenshot(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
98	        let ir = screenshotRect
99	        let scale = screenshot.size.width / ir.width
100	        let x = (point.x - ir.origin.x) * scale
101	        let y = (point.y - ir.origin.y) * scale
102	        return CGPoint(
103	            x: min(max(x, 0), screenshot.size.width),
104	            y: min(max(y, 0), screenshot.size.height)
105	        )
106	    }

108	    /// Converts a screenshot-space point to view coordinates
109	    func screenshotToView(_ point: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
110	        let ir = screenshotRect
111	        let scale = ir.width / screenshot.size.width
112	        return CGPoint(
113	            x: ir.origin.x + point.x * scale,
114	            y: ir.origin.y + point.y * scale
115	        )

118	    /// Scale factor from screenshot coords to view coords

125	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
126	        let ir = screenshotRect
127	
128	        screenshot.draw(in: ir)
129	
130	        // Draw annotations in screenshot coordinate space
131	        NSGraphicsContext.saveGraphicsState()
132	        let xform = NSAffineTransform()
133	        xform.translateX(by: ir.origin.x, yBy: ir.origin.y)
134	        let s = ir.width / screenshot.size.width
135	        xform.scaleX(by: s, yBy: s)
136	        xform.concat()
137	
138	        let editingTextIdx: Int?
139	        let activeTV: NSTextView?
140	        if case .editingText(let tv, let idx) = interactionState {
141	            editingTextIdx = idx
142	            activeTV = tv
143	        } else {
144	            editingTextIdx = nil
145	            activeTV = nil
146	        }
147	
148	        // First pass: blur annotations (between screenshot and other annotations)
149	        for (i, annotation) in annotations.enumerated() {
150	            if i == editingTextIdx { continue }
151	            if case .blur = annotation { draw(annotation) }
152	        }
153	        if let current = currentAnnotation, case .blur(let rect) = current {
154	            drawBlur(rect, cache: false)
155	        }
156	
157	        // Second pass: non-blur annotations
158	        for (i, annotation) in annotations.enumerated() {
159	            if i == editingTextIdx { continue }
160	            if case .blur = annotation { continue }
161	            draw(annotation)
162	        }
163	        if let current = currentAnnotation {
164	            if case .blur = current {} else { draw(current) }
165	        }
166	
167	        // Draw handles for hovered annotation (skip when actively editing text)
168	        if activeTV == nil, currentAnnotation == nil, let idx = hoveredAnnotationIndex,
169	           idx < annotations.count {

181	    private func drawHandles(for annotation: Annotation) {
182	        // Draw dotted border for text annotations
183	        if case .text(let origin, let width, let content, let fontSize, _) = annotation {
184	            let padding: CGFloat = 4.0 / screenshotToViewScale()
185	            let baseRect = Annotation.textBoundingRect(
186	                origin: origin, width: width, content: content, fontSize: fontSize
187	            )
188	            let rect = baseRect.insetBy(dx: -padding, dy: 0)
189	            let borderPath = NSBezierPath(rect: rect)
190	            borderPath.lineWidth = 1.5
191	            let dashPattern: [CGFloat] = [4.0, 4.0]
192	            borderPath.setLineDash(dashPattern, count: dashPattern.count, phase: 0)
193	            NSColor.red.withAlphaComponent(0.5).setStroke()
194	            borderPath.stroke()
195	        }
196	
197	        let handleRadius: CGFloat = 6.0
198	        let isText: Bool
199	        if case .text = annotation { isText = true } else { isText = false }
200	        let textPadding: CGFloat = isText ? 4.0 / screenshotToViewScale() : 0
201	        for (handle, point) in annotation.handles {
202	            var drawPoint = point
203	            if isText {
204	                drawPoint.x += (handle == .left ? -textPadding : textPadding)
205	            }
206	            let handleRect = CGRect(
207	                x: drawPoint.x - handleRadius,
208	                y: drawPoint.y - handleRadius,
209	                width: handleRadius * 2,
210	                height: handleRadius * 2
211	            )
212	            let path = NSBezierPath(ovalIn: handleRect)
213	            NSColor.white.setFill()
214	            path.fill()
215	            NSColor.red.setStroke()
216	            path.lineWidth = 2.0
217	            path.stroke()
218	        }

221	    private func drawActiveTextBorder(textView: NSTextView) {
222	        let viewFrame = textView.frame
223	        let padding: CGFloat = 4.0
224	        let topLeft = viewToScreenshot(CGPoint(x: viewFrame.minX - padding, y: viewFrame.minY))
225	        let bottomRight = viewToScreenshot(CGPoint(x: viewFrame.maxX + padding, y: viewFrame.maxY))
226	        let rect = CGRect(
227	            x: topLeft.x, y: topLeft.y,
228	            width: bottomRight.x - topLeft.x, height: bottomRight.y - topLeft.y
229	        )
230	
231	        let borderPath = NSBezierPath(rect: rect)
232	        borderPath.lineWidth = 1.5
233	        let dashPattern: [CGFloat] = [4.0, 4.0]
234	        borderPath.setLineDash(dashPattern, count: dashPattern.count, phase: 0)
235	        NSColor.red.withAlphaComponent(0.5).setStroke()
236	        borderPath.stroke()
237	
238	        let handleRadius: CGFloat = 6.0
239	        let midY = (topLeft.y + bottomRight.y) / 2
240	        for x in [topLeft.x, bottomRight.x] {
241	            let handleRect = CGRect(
242	                x: x - handleRadius, y: midY - handleRadius,
243	                width: handleRadius * 2, height: handleRadius * 2
244	            )
245	            let path = NSBezierPath(ovalIn: handleRect)
246	            NSColor.white.setFill()

258	        case .line(let from, let to, let color):

276	    private func drawArrow(from: CGPoint, to: CGPoint, color: NSColor) {
277	        color.setStroke()
278	        color.setFill()
279	
280	        let path = NSBezierPath()
281	        path.lineWidth = 3.0
282	        path.move(to: from)
283	        path.line(to: to)
284	        path.stroke()
285	
286	        // Arrowhead
287	        let angle = atan2(to.y - from.y, to.x - from.x)
288	        let headLength: CGFloat = 18.0
289	        let headAngle: CGFloat = .pi / 6
290	
291	        let p1 = CGPoint(
292	            x: to.x - headLength * cos(angle - headAngle),
293	            y: to.y - headLength * sin(angle - headAngle)
294	        )
295	        let p2 = CGPoint(
296	            x: to.x - headLength * cos(angle + headAngle),
297	            y: to.y - headLength * sin(angle + headAngle)
298	        )
299	
300	        let head = NSBezierPath()
301	        head.move(to: to)
302	        head.line(to: p1)
303	        head.line(to: p2)
304	        head.close()
305	        head.fill()
306	    }

364	    private func drawBlur(_ rect: CGRect, cache: Bool = true) {
365	        let cacheKey = BlurCacheKey(rect)
366	        if cache, let cached = blurCache[cacheKey] {
367	            cached.draw(in: rect)
368	            return
369	        }
370	
371	        guard let screenshotCG = screenshot.cgImage(forProposedRect: nil, context: nil, hints: nil)
372	        else { return }
373	
374	        let pointSize = screenshot.size
375	        let scaleX = CGFloat(screenshotCG.width) / pointSize.width
376	        let scaleY = CGFloat(screenshotCG.height) / pointSize.height
377	
378	        // CGImage.cropping(to:) uses the same top-left image coordinates as the captured screenshot.
379	        let pixelRect = CGRect(
380	            x: rect.origin.x * scaleX,
381	            y: rect.origin.y * scaleY,
382	            width: rect.width * scaleX,
383	            height: rect.height * scaleY
384	        ).integral
385	
386	        guard pixelRect.width > 0, pixelRect.height > 0,
387	              let cropped = screenshotCG.cropping(to: pixelRect)
388	        else { return }
389	
390	        let ciImage = CIImage(cgImage: cropped)
391	        let pixelSize = max(pixelRect.width, pixelRect.height) / 40
392	        let blurred = ciImage
393	            .applyingFilter("CIPhotoEffectMono")
394	            .applyingFilter("CIPixellate", parameters: [kCIInputScaleKey: pixelSize])
395	            .cropped(to: ciImage.extent)
396	
397	        guard let blurredCG = Self.blurCIContext.createCGImage(blurred, from: blurred.extent)
398	        else { return }
399	
400	        let blurredNSImage = NSImage(cgImage: blurredCG, size: rect.size)
401	        if cache { blurCache[cacheKey] = blurredNSImage }
402	        blurredNSImage.draw(in: rect)
403	    }

421	    override func mouseDown(with event: NSEvent) {
422	        let viewPoint = convert(event.locationInWindow, from: nil)
423	        let screenshotPoint = viewToScreenshot(viewPoint)
424	        dragModifiers = event.modifierFlags
425	        lastBadge = nil
426	
427	        // If editing text: clicks inside the text view are handled by it;
428	        // clicks outside finalize editing and continue to handle/body hit testing
429	        if case .editingText(let textView, _) = interactionState {
430	            if textView.frame.contains(viewPoint) {
431	                return
432	            }
433	            finalizeTextEditing()
434	        }
435	
436	        let hasDrawModifiers = dragModifiers.contains(.shift)
437	            || dragModifiers.contains(.option)
438	            || dragModifiers.contains(.command)
439	            || dragModifiers.contains(.control)
440	
441	        // Text mode: place new text annotation
442	        if isTextMode && !hasDrawModifiers {
443	            placeTextAnnotation(at: screenshotPoint)
444	            return
445	        }
446	
447	        // Exit text mode if draw modifiers pressed
448	        if isTextMode && hasDrawModifiers {
449	            isTextMode = false
450	            NSCursor.arrow.set()
451	        }
452	
453	        if !hasDrawModifiers, let (index, handle) = handleAt(screenshotPoint) {
454	            interactionState = .editingHandle(
455	                index: index, handle: handle, original: annotations[index]
456	            )
457	            return
458	        }
459	
460	        // Click on annotation body — prepare for move (if dragged) or re-edit text (if clicked)
461	        if !hasDrawModifiers, let idx = annotationBodyAt(screenshotPoint) {
462	            interactionState = .movingAnnotation(
463	                index: idx, original: annotations[idx], lastPoint: screenshotPoint
464	            )
465	            return
466	        }
467	
468	        dragOrigin = screenshotPoint
469	        interactionState = .idle
470	    }
471	
472	    override func mouseDragged(with event: NSEvent) {
473	        if case .editingText = interactionState { return }
474	
475	        let viewPoint = convert(event.locationInWindow, from: nil)
476	        let point = viewToScreenshot(viewPoint)
477	
478	        if case .movingAnnotation(let idx, let original, let lastPoint) = interactionState {
479	            guard idx < annotations.count else { interactionState = .idle; return }
480	            let dx = point.x - lastPoint.x
481	            let dy = point.y - lastPoint.y
482	            annotations[idx] = annotations[idx].offsetBy(dx: dx, dy: dy)
483	            interactionState = .movingAnnotation(index: idx, original: original, lastPoint: point)
484	            needsDisplay = true
485	            return
486	        }
487	
488	        if case .editingHandle(let idx, let handle, _) = interactionState {
489	            guard idx < annotations.count else { interactionState = .idle; return }
490	            annotations[idx] = annotations[idx].moving(handle, to: point)
491	            needsDisplay = true
492	            return
493	        }
494	
495	        let dragRect = rectFromDrag(origin: dragOrigin, current: point)
496	        if dragModifiers.contains(.command) && dragModifiers.contains(.shift) {
497	            currentAnnotation = .ellipse(rect: dragRect, color: currentColor)
498	        } else if dragModifiers.contains(.option) {
499	            currentAnnotation = .crop(rect: dragRect)
500	        } else if dragModifiers.contains(.command) {
501	            currentAnnotation = .rectangle(rect: dragRect, color: currentColor)
502	        } else if dragModifiers.contains(.control) {
503	            currentAnnotation = .blur(rect: dragRect)
504	        } else if dragModifiers.contains(.shift) {
505	            currentAnnotation = .line(from: dragOrigin, to: point, color: currentColor)
506	        } else {
507	            currentAnnotation = .arrow(from: dragOrigin, to: point, color: currentColor)
508	        }
509	
510	        needsDisplay = true
511	    }
512	
513	    override func mouseUp(with event: NSEvent) {
514	        if case .editingText = interactionState { return }
515	
516	        if case .movingAnnotation(let idx, let original, _) = interactionState {
517	            interactionState = .idle
518	            guard idx < annotations.count else { return }
519	
520	            let moved = annotations[idx] != original
521	            if !moved {
522	                // Click on text → re-edit; click on other types → no-op
523	                if case .text = annotations[idx] {
524	                    startEditingTextAnnotation(at: idx)
525	                }
526	                return
527	            }
528	
529	            // It was a drag — finalize move with undo
530	            let edited = annotations[idx]
531	            replaceAnnotation(at: idx, with: edited, old: original)
532	            return
533	        }
534	
535	        if case .editingHandle(let idx, _, let original) = interactionState {
536	            interactionState = .idle
537	            guard idx < annotations.count else { return }
538	            let edited = annotations[idx]
539	            replaceAnnotation(at: idx, with: edited, old: original)
540	            return
541	        }
542	
543	        guard let annotation = currentAnnotation else { return }
544	        currentAnnotation = nil
545	
546	        // Ignore negligible drags
547	        let point = viewToScreenshot(convert(event.locationInWindow, from: nil))
548	        if abs(point.x - dragOrigin.x) < 2, abs(point.y - dragOrigin.y) < 2 { return }
549	
550	        addAnnotation(annotation)
551	    }

553	    override func mouseMoved(with event: NSEvent) {
554	        if case .editingText = interactionState { return }
555	
556	        if isTextMode {
557	            NSCursor.iBeam.set()
558	            if hoveredAnnotationIndex != nil {
559	                hoveredAnnotationIndex = nil
560	                needsDisplay = true
561	            }
562	            return
563	        }
564	
565	        let viewPoint = convert(event.locationInWindow, from: nil)
566	        let screenshotPoint = viewToScreenshot(viewPoint)
567	
568	        let hit = hitTestAnnotations(at: screenshotPoint)
569	
570	        switch hit {
571	        case .handle(let index, let handle):
572	            let isTextEdge = (handle == .left || handle == .right)
573	            (isTextEdge ? NSCursor.resizeLeftRight : NSCursor.crosshair).set()
574	            if hoveredAnnotationIndex != index {
575	                hoveredAnnotationIndex = index
576	                needsDisplay = true
577	            }
578	        case .body(let index):
579	            NSCursor.openHand.set()
580	            if hoveredAnnotationIndex != index {
581	                hoveredAnnotationIndex = index
582	                needsDisplay = true
583	            }
584	        case .none:
585	            NSCursor.arrow.set()
586	            if hoveredAnnotationIndex != nil {
587	                hoveredAnnotationIndex = nil
588	                needsDisplay = true
589	            }
590	        }
591	    }

594	        NSCursor.arrow.set()
595	        if hoveredAnnotationIndex != nil {
596	            hoveredAnnotationIndex = nil
597	            needsDisplay = true
598	        }
599	    }

603	    override func performKeyEquivalent(with event: NSEvent) -> Bool {
604	        if case .editingText = interactionState {
605	            // Font size: Cmd+= / Cmd++ to increase, Cmd+- to decrease
606	            if event.modifierFlags.contains(.command) {
607	                if event.keyCode == 24 { // = / + key
608	                    adjustFontSize(delta: 2)
609	                    return true
610	                }
611	                if event.keyCode == 27 { // - key
612	                    adjustFontSize(delta: -2)
613	                    return true
614	                }
615	            }
616	        }
617	        if event.keyCode == 36, let action = SaveAction.action(for: event.modifierFlags) {
618	            finalizeTextEditing()
619	            performAction(action)
620	            return true
621	        }
622	        return super.performKeyEquivalent(with: event)
623	    }

625	    override func keyDown(with event: NSEvent) {
626	        // When text view is active, let it handle all keys
627	        if case .editingText = interactionState { return }
628	
629	        if event.keyCode == 53 { // ESC
630	            handleEscape()
631	            return
632	        }
633	
634	        // Delete / Forward Delete — remove hovered annotation
635	        if event.keyCode == 51 || event.keyCode == 117 {
636	            if let idx = hoveredAnnotationIndex {
637	                removeAnnotation(at: idx)
638	                hoveredAnnotationIndex = nil
639	            }
640	            return
641	        }
642	
643	        let noModifiers = event.modifierFlags.intersection(.deviceIndependentFlagsMask) == []
644	        if noModifiers, handleUnmodifiedKey(event.keyCode) { return }
645	
646	        super.keyDown(with: event)
647	    }

649	    private func handleEscape() {
650	        if isTextMode {
651	            isTextMode = false
652	            NSCursor.arrow.set()
653	            return
654	        }
655	        for i in stride(from: annotations.count - 1, through: 0, by: -1) {
656	            if case .crop = annotations[i] { removeAnnotation(at: i) }
657	        }
658	    }

660	    /// Handles single-key shortcuts (no modifiers). Returns true if the key was consumed.
661	    private func handleUnmodifiedKey(_ keyCode: UInt16) -> Bool {
662	        switch keyCode {
663	        case 32: // U — insert UTC timestamp at cursor
664	            insertTimestamp()
665	            return true
666	        case 17: // T — toggle text mode
667	            isTextMode.toggle()
668	            (isTextMode ? NSCursor.iBeam : NSCursor.arrow).set()
669	            return true
670	        case 8: // C — toggle color (red/blue)
671	            toggleColor()
672	            return true
673	        default:
674	            // Digit keys — place numbered badge at cursor
675	            if let digit = Self.digitKeyCodes[keyCode] {
676	                placeBadge(digit: digit)
677	                return true
678	            }
679	            return false
680	        }
681	    }

683	    /// Layout-independent key codes for the digit row, 1 through 0
684	    private static let digitKeyCodes: [UInt16: Int] = [
685	        18: 1, 19: 2, 20: 3, 21: 4, 23: 5, 22: 6, 26: 7, 28: 8, 25: 9, 29: 0
686	    ]

688	    /// Places a numbered badge at the cursor. A digit pressed shortly after the
689	    /// previous one extends that badge's number instead (1, 2 → 12).
690	    private func placeBadge(digit: Int) {
691	        let now = Date()
692	        if let last = lastBadge,
693	           now.timeIntervalSince(last.time) < Self.badgeCombineInterval,
694	           last.index < annotations.count,
695	           case .badge(let center, let number, let color) = annotations[last.index],
696	           number < 10 {
697	            let combined = Annotation.badge(center: center, number: number * 10 + digit, color: color)
698	            replaceAnnotation(at: last.index, with: combined, old: annotations[last.index])
699	            lastBadge = (last.index, now)
700	            return
701	        }
702	
703	        guard let window = window else { return }
704	        let viewPoint = convert(window.mouseLocationOutsideOfEventStream, from: nil)
705	        let screenshotPoint = viewToScreenshot(viewPoint)
706	        addAnnotation(.badge(center: screenshotPoint, number: digit, color: currentColor))
707	        lastBadge = (annotations.count - 1, now)
708	    }

710	    /// Toggles the hovered annotation's color, or the drawing color when nothing is hovered
711	    private func toggleColor() {
712	        if let idx = hoveredAnnotationIndex, idx < annotations.count,
713	           let color = annotations[idx].color {
714	            currentColor = color.toggled
715	            replaceAnnotation(at: idx, with: annotations[idx].withColor(currentColor),
716	                              old: annotations[idx])
717	            return
718	        }
719	        currentColor = currentColor.toggled
720	    }

752	    private func placeTextAnnotation(at screenshotPoint: CGPoint) {
753	        let scale = screenshotToViewScale()
754	        let viewOrigin = screenshotToView(screenshotPoint)
755	        let viewWidth = 300 * scale
756	        let viewFontSize = textFontSize * scale
757	
758	        let frame = CGRect(x: viewOrigin.x, y: viewOrigin.y, width: viewWidth, height: viewFontSize * 1.5)
759	        let textView = createTextView(frame: frame, fontSize: viewFontSize)

766	        guard case .text(let origin, let width, let content, let fontSize, let color) = annotations[index]
767	        else { return }

771	        let viewWidth = width * scale
772	        let viewFontSize = fontSize * scale
773

816	    func finalizeTextEditing() {
817	        guard case .editingText(let textView, let existingIndex) = interactionState else { return }
818	        let content = textView.string
819	        let viewFrame = textView.frame
820	
821	        textView.removeFromSuperview()
822	        interactionState = .idle
823	        window?.makeFirstResponder(self)
824	
825	        // Convert view frame back to screenshot coords
826	        let scale = screenshotToViewScale()
827	        let screenshotOrigin = viewToScreenshot(CGPoint(x: viewFrame.minX, y: viewFrame.minY))
828	        let screenshotWidth = viewFrame.width / scale
829	
830	        if let idx = existingIndex {
831	            if content.isEmpty {
832	                removeAnnotation(at: idx)
833	            } else {
834	                let newAnnotation = Annotation.text(
835	                    origin: screenshotOrigin, width: screenshotWidth,
836	                    content: content, fontSize: textFontSize, color: currentColor
837	                )
838	                let old = annotations[idx]
839	                replaceAnnotation(at: idx, with: newAnnotation, old: old)
840	            }
841	        } else {
842	            if !content.isEmpty {
843	                let annotation = Annotation.text(
844	                    origin: screenshotOrigin, width: screenshotWidth,
845	                    content: content, fontSize: textFontSize, color: currentColor
846	                )
847	                addAnnotation(annotation)
848	            }
849	        }
850	
851	        isTextMode = false
852	        NSCursor.arrow.set()
853	        needsDisplay = true
854	    }

856	    private func insertTimestamp() {
857	        guard let window = window else { return }
858	        let windowPoint = window.mouseLocationOutsideOfEventStream
859	        let viewPoint = convert(windowPoint, from: nil)
860	        let screenshotPoint = viewToScreenshot(viewPoint)
861	
862	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
863	        formatter.dateFormat = "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss 'UTC'"
864	        formatter.timeZone = TimeZone(identifier: "UTC")
865	        let timestamp = formatter.string(from: captureDate)
866	
867	        let font = NSFont.boldSystemFont(ofSize: textFontSize)
868	        let textWidth = (timestamp as NSString).size(withAttributes: [.font: font]).width + 4
869	
870	        let annotation = Annotation.text(
871	            origin: screenshotPoint, width: textWidth,
872	            content: timestamp, fontSize: textFontSize, color: currentColor
873	        )
874	        addAnnotation(annotation)
875	        needsDisplay = true
876	    }

878	    private func adjustFontSize(delta: CGFloat) {
879	        let newSize = max(textFontSize + delta, 8)
880	        textFontSize = newSize
881	        guard case .editingText(let textView, _) = interactionState else { return }
882	        let scale = screenshotToViewScale()
883	        let viewFontSize = newSize * scale
884	        let font = NSFont.boldSystemFont(ofSize: viewFontSize)
885	        textView.font = font
886	        textView.typingAttributes = [.font: font, .foregroundColor: currentColor.nsColor]
887	        // Re-apply font to all existing text
888	        if !textView.string.isEmpty {
889	            let range = NSRange(location: 0, length: (textView.string as NSString).length)
890	            textView.textStorage?.addAttribute(.font, value: font, range: range)
891	        }
892	        needsDisplay = true
893	    }

903	
904	    /// Single-pass hit test: checks handles first, then body, for each annotation top-to-bottom
905	    private func hitTestAnnotations(at point: CGPoint) -> AnnotationHitTestResult {
906	        let ir = screenshotRect
907	        let scale = ir.width / screenshot.size.width
908	        let handleHitRadius: CGFloat = 10.0 / scale
909	        let bodyHitRadius: CGFloat = 5.0 / scale
910	
911	        for i in stride(from: annotations.count - 1, through: 0, by: -1) {
912	            // Check handles first
913	            var bestHandle: AnnotationHandle?
914	            var bestDist = CGFloat.greatestFiniteMagnitude
915	            for (handle, handlePoint) in annotations[i].handles {
916	                let dist = hypot(point.x - handlePoint.x, point.y - handlePoint.y)
917	                if dist <= handleHitRadius && dist < bestDist {
918	                    bestDist = dist
919	                    bestHandle = handle
920	                }
921	            }
922	            if let handle = bestHandle {
923	                return .handle(index: i, handle: handle)
924	            }
925	            // Check body
926	            if annotations[i].bodyContains(point, hitRadius: bodyHitRadius) {
927	                return .body(index: i)
928	            }
929	        }
930	        return .none
931	    }

933	    /// Returns the annotation index and handle at the given screenshot-space point
934	    func handleAt(_ point: CGPoint) -> (index: Int, handle: AnnotationHandle)? {
935	        if case .handle(let index, let handle) = hitTestAnnotations(at: point) {
936	            return (index, handle)
937	        }
938	        return nil
939	    }

1018	    private func compositeAsCGImage() -> CGImage? {
1019	        guard let screenshotCG = screenshot.cgImage(
1020	            forProposedRect: nil, context: nil, hints: nil
1021	        ) else { return nil }
1022	
1023	        let pixelWidth = screenshotCG.width
1024	        let pixelHeight = screenshotCG.height
1025	        let pointSize = screenshot.size
1026	        let colorSpace = screenshotCG.colorSpace ?? CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB()
1027	
1028	        guard let ctx = CGContext(
1029	            data: nil,
1030	            width: pixelWidth,
1031	            height: pixelHeight,
1032	            bitsPerComponent: 8,
1033	            bytesPerRow: 0,
1034	            space: colorSpace,
1035	            bitmapInfo: CGImageAlphaInfo.premultipliedFirst.rawValue
1036	                | CGBitmapInfo.byteOrder32Little.rawValue
1037	        ) else { return nil }
1038	
1039	        // Draw screenshot at full pixel resolution (bottom-left origin, no transform)
1040	        ctx.draw(screenshotCG, in: CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: pixelWidth, height: pixelHeight))
1041	
1042	        // Transform to top-left origin in point coordinates for annotations
1043	        ctx.saveGState()
1044	        ctx.translateBy(x: 0, y: CGFloat(pixelHeight))
1045	        ctx.scaleBy(
1046	            x: CGFloat(pixelWidth) / pointSize.width,
1047	            y: -CGFloat(pixelHeight) / pointSize.height
1048	        )
1049	
1050	        let nsContext = NSGraphicsContext(cgContext: ctx, flipped: true)
1051	        NSGraphicsContext.saveGraphicsState()
1052	        NSGraphicsContext.current = nsContext
1053	
1054	        // First pass: blur annotations (between screenshot and other annotations)
1055	        for annotation in annotations {
1056	            if case .blur = annotation { draw(annotation) }
1057	        }
1058	
1059	        // Second pass: non-blur, non-crop annotations
1060	        for annotation in annotations {
1061	            if case .crop = annotation { continue }
1062	            if case .blur = annotation { continue }
1063	            draw(annotation)
1064	        }
1065	
1066	        NSGraphicsContext.restoreGraphicsState()
1067	        ctx.restoreGState()
1068	
1069	        guard var cgImage = ctx.makeImage() else { return nil }
1070	
1071	        // Apply crop if present
1072	        if let cropAnnotation = annotations.first(where: {
1073	            if case .crop = $0 { return true }; return false
1074	        }), case .crop(let cropRect) = cropAnnotation {
1075	            let scaleX = CGFloat(pixelWidth) / pointSize.width
1076	            let scaleY = CGFloat(pixelHeight) / pointSize.height
1077	            let pixelCropRect = CGRect(
1078	                x: cropRect.origin.x * scaleX,
1079	                y: cropRect.origin.y * scaleY,
1080	                width: cropRect.width * scaleX,
1081	                height: cropRect.height * scaleY
1082	            )
1083	            if let cropped = cgImage.cropping(to: pixelCropRect) {
1084	                cgImage = cropped
1085	            }
1086	        }
1087	
1088	        return cgImage
1089	    }

216	    /// (e.g. cloud upload without a key configured), so the caller can keep the window open.
217	    @discardableResult
218	    func handleAction(_ action: SaveAction, cgImage: CGImage, captureDate: Date) -> Bool {
219	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
220	        formatter.dateFormat = "yyyyMMddHHmmss"
221	        let filename = "skryn-\(formatter.string(from: captureDate)).png"
222	
223	        switch action {
224	        case .clipboard:
225	            let nsImage = NSImage(
226	                cgImage: cgImage, size: NSSize(width: cgImage.width, height: cgImage.height)
227	            )
228	            NSPasteboard.general.clearContents()
229	            NSPasteboard.general.writeObjects([nsImage])
230	            return true
231	
232	        case .local:
233	            guard let pngData = pngData(from: cgImage) else {
234	                reportSaveFailure("Save failed: could not create PNG data")
235	                return false
236	            }
237	            return saveLocally(pngData: pngData, filename: filename)
238	
239	        case .cloud:
240	            guard let publicKey = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: "uploadcarePublicKey"),
241	                  !publicKey.isEmpty else {
242	                NSSound.beep()
243	                return false
244	            }
245	            guard let pngData = pngData(from: cgImage) else {
246	                reportSaveFailure("Upload failed: could not create PNG data")
247	                return false
248	            }
249	            return uploadToCloud(pngData: pngData, filename: filename, publicKey: publicKey)
250	        }
251	    }

324	    /// Shared upload logic: animates icon, runs async upload, updates history, handles errors.
325	    /// If `fallbackSave` is provided, saves locally on upload failure.
326	    private func performUpload(fileData: Data, filename: String, contentType: String,
327	                               publicKey: String, fallbackSave: Data?) {
328	        let uploadID = UUID()
329	        let cdnBase = UploadcareService.cdnBase(forPublicKey: publicKey)
330	        if uploadTasks.isEmpty {
331	            uploadFailed = false
332	            lastUploadError = nil
333	        }
334	        startIconAnimation()
335	
336	        let task = Task {
337	            do {
338	                let cdnURL = try await UploadcareService.upload(
339	                    fileData: fileData, filename: filename, contentType: contentType,
340	                    publicKey: publicKey, cdnBase: cdnBase
341	                )
342	                await MainActor.run {
343	                    UploadHistory.updateCDNURL(for: filename, url: cdnURL)
344	                    copyToClipboard(cdnURL)
345	                    if !self.uploadFailed {
346	                        self.lastUploadError = nil
347	                    }
348	                    self.finishUpload(id: uploadID, failed: false)
349	                    print("Uploaded: \(cdnURL)")
350	                }
351	            } catch {
352	                await MainActor.run {
353	                    self.lastUploadError = "Upload failed: \(error.localizedDescription)"
354	                    if let pngData = fallbackSave {
355	                        self.saveLocally(pngData: pngData, filename: filename)
356	                    }
357	                    self.finishUpload(id: uploadID, failed: true)
358	                    print("Upload failed: \(error.localizedDescription)")
359	                }
360	            }
361	        }
362	        uploadTasks[uploadID] = task
363	    }

content.text:
I read every source file but didn't change anything, and I haven't reproduced any of these at runtime. Findings are ranked by impact.

## Bugs

**1. Cmd+Z while editing text undoes annotations, not the text, and can crash.** `AnnotationView.swift:722`
- The Undo menu item sends `undo:` with no target. NSTextView doesn't implement `undo:`, so the call climbs to the parent `AnnotationView.undo(_:)`, which undoes on the annotation stack.
- As a result, typing in a text box and pressing Cmd+Z removes your last arrow or other annotation. The text view's own undo manager is never used.
- Crash path: click an existing text annotation to re-edit it, press Cmd+Z (this removes that annotation), then press Enter. `finalizeTextEditing` then runs `annotations[idx]` at line 838 before any bounds check, which crashes.
- Fix: in `undo`/`redo`, if the state is `.editingText(tv, _)`, send the call to `tv.undoManager` instead.

**2. Opening Settings or About while the annotation window is up removes Cmd+Z, Cmd+W and Cmd+Q.** `AppDelegate.swift:446, 464`
- `installEditOnlyMenu()` replaces the full main menu.
- When the panel closes, `windowWillClose` doesn't restore it, because `annotationWindow` is still open.
- Fix: always install the full menu. Items with no responder in the chain disable themselves anyway, and this also removes the duplicated Edit-menu code.

**3. Pressing the hotkey twice quickly can open two annotation windows.** `AppDelegate.swift:565, 577`
- `annotationWindow == nil` is checked before the async capture starts, so a second press during the capture passes the check too.
- The second window replaces the first in `annotationWindow`, and the first stays on screen orphaned: it can't be closed through the delegate path and the app never goes back to the accessory policy.
- Fix: add an `isCapturing` flag.

**4. After cropping, a plain drag inside the crop area moves the crop instead of drawing an arrow.** `Annotation.swift:181`
- The crop's hit area is its whole rectangle, and the crop area is exactly where you want to draw. Blur regions and rectangles behave the same way.
- This may be intentional, but I'd hit-test only the border for crop and rectangle.

**5. Blur is weak on small regions.** `AnnotationView.swift:391`
- The pixel block size is `max(w,h)/40`. For a small field, such as an 80×16pt password on a Retina screen, that gives about 4px blocks over roughly 28px-tall text, which may stay readable.
- Fix: set a minimum block size, e.g. `max(…, 10 * scale)`.

**6. Filenames and the timestamp use the user's calendar.** `AppDelegate.swift:219`, `AnnotationView.swift:862`
- Neither `DateFormatter` sets `locale = en_US_POSIX`.
- With a Buddhist or Japanese calendar you get years like `2569`, and some region settings can alter the output.

**7. Smaller issues:**
- A rejected file drop resets a red "upload failed" icon to normal after 2 seconds (`AppDelegate.swift:307`).
- `hoveredAnnotationIndex` goes stale after undo/redo until the mouse moves. Pressing C or Delete right after undo can hit a different annotation.
- Annotations can be dragged fully off the canvas, and then there's no way to grab them back (`offsetBy` isn't clamped).
- CLAUDE.md says digits combine within 1s, but the code uses 0.5s (`AnnotationView.swift:50`).

## Improvements

- **Clipboard:** `writeObjects([nsImage])` puts only TIFF on the pasteboard. Adding PNG data too (`.png` type) makes pasting into browser apps more reliable.
- **Capture failures are silent:** if Screen Recording permission is missing (which your unsigned-update flow causes), clicking the icon does nothing. Showing the red icon plus a menu message pointing to System Settings would save confusion.
- **Blur cache:** the whole cache is cleared on every annotation change, so adding an arrow re-renders every blur. Moving or resizing a blur also caches one image per mouse-move frame. It would be better to skip caching during drags and remove only entries whose rect no longer exists. Separately, fetching the screenshot's CGImage once, instead of calling `screenshot.cgImage(...)` on each blur draw, would help.
- **Launch at login:** `try? service.register()` swallows errors, including the "requires approval" case.

## Refactors

- **UserDefaults keys and defaults** are string literals repeated across AppDelegate, SettingsPanel and SaveAction. The hotkey default `kVK_ANSI_5` / `cmdKey|shiftKey` appears in 4 places. A single `Defaults` enum would cover it. `SettingsPanel.loadSettings` also duplicates `SaveModifier.configured(forKey:default:)`.
- **Dead code:**
  - `UploadcareService.normalizeCdnBase` / `defaultCdnBase` are only used by tests, since the CDN base is now derived from the key.
  - The `upload(pngData:)` wrapper is unused, and `contentType` is always `"image/png"`.
  - `onHotkeyRecorded` is never assigned.
  - `textAnnotationAt` is test-only.
- **`await MainActor.run`** in `performUpload` is redundant: the delegate is main-actor isolated, so the Task already runs there.
- **Handle and dashed-border drawing** is duplicated between `drawHandles` and `drawActiveTextBorder` and could share a helper.
- **`compositeAsCGImage`'s crop lookup** can be simplified to `annotations.lazy.compactMap { if case .crop(let r) = $0 { r } else { nil } }.first`.

46:**Numbered badges:** Digit keys 1–0 (no modifiers) place a `.badge` (filled circle + white number) at the cursor. A digit pressed within 1s of the previous one combines into a multi-digit number (1, 2 → 12; capped at two digits via the `number < 10` guard). Badges have no handles; they move via body drag.
54:**Drag-to-move:** Any annotation can be repositioned by dragging its body. `bodyContains(_:hitRadius:)` does hit testing (point-to-segment distance for lines/arrows, rect containment for rectangles/crop/text). `annotationBodyAt(_:)` finds the topmost hit. Click-without-drag on text opens re-editing; on other types it's a no-op. Move uses `offsetBy(dx:dy:)` with undo support.
66:**Settings panel:** `SettingsPanel.swift` — NSPanel with three save action rows (local folder, clipboard, cloud upload), each with an `NSPopUpButton` to choose the modifier key (Cmd/Opt/Ctrl). Auto-swap prevents duplicate modifiers. Also has a hotkey recorder (`HotkeyRecorderButton.swift`) and launch-at-login checkbox. Opened via right-click menu "Settings…" (⌘,). Uses `installEditOnlyMenu()` + `.regular` activation policy so Cmd+V works in the key field. `windowWillClose` only reverts to `.accessory` when both annotation window and settings panel are nil.
71:**Right-click menu structure:**
72:- Recent Uploads submenu (only if uploads exist) / error message (if any) / "Settings…" (⌘,, opens settings panel) / Quit
101:- Borderless windows don't support `performClose(_:)` — Close routes through `AppDelegate.closeAnnotationWindow()` instead.

lines: - **One main menu for every window.** `installMainMenu()` is used for the annotation window, settings, and about panels. Don't install a reduced menu for panels — opening one while annotating would strip Undo/Close from the annotation window.

- **Undo while editing text.** NSTextView doesn't implement `undo:`/`redo:`, so the menu action reaches `AnnotationView.undo(_:)`, which forwards to the text view's own undo manager during `.editingText`.
- **UserDefaults keys** live in `Defaults` (and `SaveAction.defaultsKey` for modifiers) in `SettingsPanel.swift` — don't use string literals.

+- **Blur:** pixel blocks are at least `minBlurBlockSize` (10pt) so small regions stay unreadable. `blurCache` is keyed by rect and pruned (not cleared) on annotation changes; a blur being dragged renders uncached so intermediate frames don't accumulate.
+- **Clipboard** writes one `NSPasteboardItem` with both PNG and TIFF data.
- `AppDelegate` is `@MainActor`; `Task {}` inside it runs on the main actor, so no `MainActor.run` hops are needed.
- `NSEvent.modifierFlags` (static) reads current keyboard state; `event.modifierFlags` (instance) reads state at event time. Always use the instance property for tool locking.
- When renaming variables, check ALL references in the same method — secondary uses are easy to miss.

content.text:
Everything you picked is done. The build is clean, all tests pass, lint shows only the two complexity warnings that were already there, and nothing is committed. I haven't run the app itself, so the manual checks at the end still need doing.

**Bugs**
1. **Undo while typing text:** Cmd+Z now undoes the text you typed, and Cmd+Shift+Z redoes it. A quick test confirmed the text box can't handle Undo itself, so the command falls through to the drawing view, which now hands it to the text box. I can't explain why your test didn't undo an annotation either. If there were no annotations yet, that would account for it, but that's a guess.
2. **Settings opened mid-annotation:** a realistic case is right-clicking the menu bar icon during an annotation to paste an Uploadcare key. Afterwards Cmd+Z, Cmd+W and Cmd+Q stopped working in the annotation window, because Settings put in a smaller menu. Now every window uses the same full menu, and Cmd+W closes whichever window is in front. The duplicate menu code is gone too.
3. **Double hotkey press:** you couldn't reproduce this, but I added a cheap guard so a second capture can't start while one is still running.
4. **Drawing inside shapes:** rectangles, ellipses and the crop can now be grabbed only near their outline. You can draw inside them freely. Blur regions and text still move when you drag anywhere inside them.
5. **Blur:** each pixel block is now at least 10pt, so small regions like a password field can't be read. Larger regions look the same as before.
6. **Dates:** filenames and the timestamp now always use the standard calendar and fixed formatting. The timestamp was already UTC. Filenames still use local time. Did you want those in UTC too? It's a one-line change.
7. **Other fixes:**
   - The hover highlight is recalculated after undo, redo and delete, so C and Delete act on the right annotation.
   - Dragging annotations fully off the canvas: I was wrong about this. The pointer position is already kept inside the image, so part of the annotation always stays on it. No change needed.
   - CLAUDE.md now says 0.5s for combining badge digits, and I updated it for everything else above.

**Improvements**
- **Clipboard:** the copied image now includes PNG as well as TIFF.
- **Capture failures:** the icon turns red with a beep, and the right-click menu shows the error. If the Screen Recording permission is missing, the menu also has "Open Screen Recording Settings…" and a hint to remove Skryn and add it again.
- **Blur cache:** it now drops only entries for blurs that no longer exist, instead of clearing everything on each change. A blur you're dragging isn't cached frame by frame.
- **Launch at login:** errors now appear in an alert. If macOS needs your approval, you get a button that opens Login Items.

**Refactors**
- All settings keys and default values now live in one `Defaults` enum.
- The unused CDN-address code and its tests are gone, and there's now a single PNG upload function.
- `AppDelegate` is now explicitly tied to the main thread (`@MainActor`), which made the extra main-thread hops in the upload code unnecessary. A check showed this wasn't guaranteed before.
- Handle and border drawing share helpers, and the rest is smaller cleanup of duplicated code.

**Please check by hand:**
- Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z while typing in a text box.
- Open Settings during an annotation, close it, then try Cmd+Z and Cmd+W.
- Draw an arrow inside a crop.
- Paste a clipboard copy into a browser.
- Turn launch at login on and off.

message.content: Do you foresee any issues with just press T and start typing, w/o additional click?

content.text:
It's a small, safe change. Badges and the U timestamp already appear at the cursor the same way. A few things to handle:

1. **Old habit of pressing T, then clicking somewhere else.** Today that click places the text. After the change, T opens an empty text box at the cursor, and a click elsewhere closes it. Empty text is thrown away, so the box just disappears and the click does nothing. Fix: while the box is still empty, a click elsewhere moves it to the click point. Both habits then work.

2. **Pressing T over existing text** would stack a new text box on top of it. It would be better for T to open the hovered text for editing, the same as clicking it.

3. **Cursor outside the window.** The box would appear clamped at the window edge. Badges already behave this way, so it's consistent, just slightly odd.

4. **Holding T a little too long.** Key repeat could type a stray "t" into the new box. It's rare, and ignoring repeated key presses fixes it.

5. **Losing "press T again to cancel."** Once the box has focus, T types a letter. Esc on an empty box already discards it, so nothing is lost. The About panel and website just need to say Esc.

It also simplifies the code. The separate text mode, its I-beam cursor and its special cases in the mouse handlers would all go away.

I'd do it with fixes 1 and 2. Want me to go ahead and update the About panel and website text too?

lines: **Keyboard shortcuts** are handled via the installed `NSApp.mainMenu` (Cmd+W, Cmd+Z, Cmd+Shift+Z, Cmd+Q) for proper cross-layout support. ESC uses `keyDown` (layout-independent keyCode). Modifier+Enter uses `performKeyEquivalent` — the menu system intercepts modifier combos before they reach `keyDown`. Each of the three save actions (local, clipboard, cloud) has a configurable modifier key (Cmd/Opt/Ctrl) stored in UserDefaults. `SaveAction.action(for:)` maps the pressed modifier to the correct action.

-**Tool selection:** Modifier keys at `mouseDown` time determine the tool — plain drag = arrow, Shift = line, Command = rectangle, Shift+Command = ellipse, Option = crop, Control = blur. T key enters text mode (I-beam cursor, click to place). Only one crop allowed at a time.

+**Tool selection:** Modifier keys at `mouseDown` time determine the tool — plain drag = arrow, Shift = line, Command = rectangle, Shift+Command = ellipse, Option = crop, Control = blur. T key opens a text editor at the cursor. Only one crop allowed at a time.

**Color:** Annotations carry an `AnnotationColor` (red/blue) associated value; crop and blur are colorless. C key toggles the color of the hovered annotation, or the drawing color (`currentColor`) when nothing is hovered. The text editor inherits `currentColor`.

**Numbered badges:** Digit keys 1–0 (no modifiers) place a `.badge` (filled circle + white number) at the cursor. A digit pressed within 0.5s (`badgeCombineInterval`) of the previous one combines into a multi-digit number (1, 2 → 12; capped at two digits via the `number < 10` guard). Badges have no handles; they move via body drag.

-**Text annotations:** T key toggles text mode. Click to place an `IsolatedUndoTextView` (red bold text, transparent background). Enter finalizes, Shift+Enter inserts newline, ESC finalizes. Cmd+=/Cmd+- adjusts font size. Click on finalized text to re-edit. Text width is resizable via left/right edge handles. `IsolatedUndoTextView` is a private NSTextView subclass with its own undo manager — this prevents text-editing undo operations from leaking into AnnotationView's undo stack (which would crash on Cmd+Z after the text view is removed). `finalizeTextEditing()` converts the NSTextView back to a `.text` annotation. The Edit menu (Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All) in `AppDelegate.installMainMenu()` enables clipboard support in the text view via responder chain.

+**Text annotations:** T places an `IsolatedUndoTextView` (bold text in `currentColor`, transparent background) at the cursor and starts editing immediately; T over an existing text annotation re-edits it instead (`startTextAtCursor`). While the new box is still empty, a plain click elsewhere moves it there (keeps the old "T, then click" habit working). Auto-repeat of the T key is swallowed by the text view (`swallowsRepeatOfKeyCode`). Enter finalizes, Shift+Enter inserts newline, ESC finalizes; empty text is discarded. The Edit menu (Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All) in `AppDelegate.installMainMenu()` enables clipboard support in the text view via responder chain.

-**Interaction state:** AnnotationView uses a single `InteractionState` enum (`.idle`, `.editingHandle`, `.movingAnnotation`, `.editingText`) instead of parallel optional variables. This makes invalid state combinations impossible. Persistent state (`isTextMode`, `textFontSize`, `hoveredAnnotationIndex`, `currentAnnotation`, `dragOrigin`/`dragModifiers`) remains as separate properties since they're orthogonal to the interaction state.

- Clipboard gets PNG in addition to TIFF
- Launch-at-login errors and approval state are shown

Refactors:
- Defaults enum for UserDefaults keys and default values
- Blur cache is pruned instead of cleared; dragged blurs render uncached
- Remove unused Uploadcare CDN normalization and upload overloads
- AppDelegate is @MainActor; drop MainActor.run hops
- Shared handle/border drawing helpers

Bump version to 0.1.5.

## What's new

- **Numbered badges** — press digit keys `1`–`0` to drop a numbered badge at the cursor; a second digit within half a second makes a two-digit number.

- **Type text at the cursor** — press `T` and start typing right away, no extra click. `T` over existing text edits it; while the new box is still empty, clicking elsewhere moves it there.
- **Draw inside shapes** — rectangles, ellipses, and the crop area are now grabbed only by their outline, so you can draw arrows inside them.
- **Stronger blur** — small blurred regions (like a password field) now use larger blocks and stay unreadable.
- **Screen Recording help** — if capture fails because permission is missing, the icon turns red and the menu offers "Open Screen Recording Settings…".
- **Better clipboard compatibility** — copied screenshots include PNG, so pasting into browsers and web apps works more reliably.
- **UTC filenames** — saved files are named by UTC time, using the standard calendar regardless of system locale.

## Fixes

- `⌘Z` / `⌘⇧Z` while typing now undo/redo the text itself.
- Opening Settings or About during an annotation no longer disables `⌘Z`, `⌘W`, and `⌘Q` in the annotation window.
- `C` and `⌫` right after undo/redo now act on the annotation actually under the cursor.
- Launch at login now reports errors, and prompts you when macOS needs approval in Login Items.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/rsedykh/skryn/compare/v0.1.4...v0.1.5

- **The tag would be left behind.** `v0.1.5` would still point at the old commit, which would no longer be on `main`, unless the tag is moved and pushed again as well.

A separate small commit on top avoids both. It only changes CLAUDE.md, so the release is unaffected. Git writes were blocked for me earlier, so here's the command to run:

```
! cd /Users/rsedykh/GitHub/skryn && git commit -am "Document hand-written release notes in CLAUDE.md" && git push origin main
```

If you still want it folded into the release commit, the steps are:
1. Amend the commit.
2. Force-push `main`.
3. Move the `v0.1.5` tag to the new commit and force-push the tag.

The release asset doesn't need rebuilding, since only CLAUDE.md changes. Tell me if you want that route.
